visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 better matches the projectile-range problem by showing the full parabolic trajectory from ground launch to ground impact with axes and flight-time equations, while Lesson 1’s mid-frame component triangle is correct but only visualizes the velocity split and not the actual range/projectile path being solved.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a concrete, wired fill-in gate after act_decomposition with a real prompt, expected answer, hint, and remediation path, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no evidence of any functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has more natural, clearly paced narration with structured transitions, while Lesson 1 is understandable but begins with an awkward fragment and is denser and less smoothly paced.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that mostly coincide with the narration’s references to setup, vectors, trajectory, decomposition, equations, and range, while Lesson 1 has no beat or cue timing data at all, making its visual-narration synchronization impossible to verify and therefore worse on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is equally mathematically correct but teaches the concept more clearly by explicitly deriving the flight-time equation, identifying the two time roots, connecting vertical and horizontal motion, and deriving the range formula, whereas Lesson 1 is correct but more compressed and less pedagogically scaffolded.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a more cohesive, centered, professional layout with consistent dark styling and no visible playback UI, while Lesson 1 has oversized/poorly positioned title text, nearly invisible subtitle text, excessive empty space, and intrusive video controls/subtitle overlays that reduce polish.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents favored Lesson 2, with consistently moderate-to-high confidence. Lesson 2 was judged stronger visually because it depicts the full projectile trajectory and range context, much stronger interactively due to a functioning fill-in checkpoint, better narrated with smoother pacing, better synchronized through timed visual cues, clearer conceptually by deriving flight time and range more explicitly, and more polished in layout and presentation. Since every dimension preferred Lesson 2 and several did so with high confidence, the overall winner is clearly Lesson 2.
